dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 1.8 Earth-radius dip every 2.56 days with a flat bottom and no credible neighbour within a pixel able to mimic it, and the star's size matches the transit duration. The large scatter in published depths is only between different pipelines (QLP deep, SPOC shallow) and is steady within each, so the signal is a planet-sized dip on the target worthy of follow-up to refine depth and rule out a faint distant blend.
